name: crew
description: Makes the main session a lead that delegates to six specialist subagents: code-reader and research on Haiku; designer, developer and tester on Sonnet; architect on Opus. It also shows a live HUD of the crew's work (the session, the quota, the active plan's next steps, the running agents, the architect's verdicts and a log) in a side pane or a band above the prompt. With the jevKey option set (a TypeSafe key), Jev may move each call's model one step (the architect stays on Opus) and raise its effort to high; that sends a redacted, truncated prompt to api.typesafe.ai. With the nativeCodex option set and a local proxy as ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, roles also get crew:<role>-codex subagent types that run on a Codex model through that proxy, which sends what those subagents read and write to OpenAI; with quotaRouting on, a call may move to its role's twin when Codex has more weekly headroom.

jevKey.title: Jev API key (TypeSafe)
jevKey.description: Setting this key turns Jev routing on; leaving it empty turns it off. With a key, Jev (TypeSafe) chooses the model and effort of each crew:* Agent call, one step from the agent's default and never below the architect's Opus floor or medium effort, and the choice shows in the task's description. The call's description and its prompt (secrets and paths removed, cut to 4000 characters) are sent to api.typesafe.ai. The agent type stays the one chosen (only quotaRouting may move a call to its role's Codex twin), and a call that names a model keeps it. The key is sent only in the Authorization header and is never logged or stored by the plugin. A repository's own settings cannot supply it.

nativeCodex.title: Native Codex models per role
nativeCodex.description: Registers a crew:<role>-codex subagent type for each role=model pair, e.g. developer=gpt-x,tester=gpt-y, running on that model with the role's prompt, tools and write lane. The model is reached through a local proxy at ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, so the types are registered only when that URL is an http URL on a loopback address (127.0.0.0/8, ::1 or localhost); with any other base URL, or none, nothing is registered. What those subagents read and write is sent to OpenAI through the proxy. With a jevKey, Jev may size their effort when the host sends one (never the model) from the redacted prompt, as for the other roles. The quotaRouting option can also send a call to a twin. Empty by default.

quotaRouting.title: Quota-aware provider routing
quotaRouting.description: Lets crew send a crew:<role> call to the same role's Codex twin when Codex has more 7-day headroom than Claude, which sends that call's work to OpenAI through the local proxy. It needs registered twins (the nativeCodex option) and reads the proxy's status with its secret header; off by default.

placement.title: Placement
placement.description: Where the panel shows before you pick with /crew:panel. side: the pane beside the transcript (inline above the prompt on a narrow terminal or the main screen). prompt: a summary band above the prompt, which yields to any other plugin's band (terminal and desktop only).

openOnStart.title: Open on start
openOnStart.description: Show the panel when a session starts and you have not picked yet with /crew:panel; once you have, your pick wins.

motion.title: Motion
motion.description: Animate the connectors while work flows, or keep everything still; the clocks tick either way.

colors.title: Colors
colors.description: theme: only your Claude Code theme's colors (they follow its light, dark and colour-blind themes); roles are told apart by name and glyph. roles: a color per crew role, tuned for dark terminals.
